{[When you think of a sand dune, you probably picture a barren pile of lifeless sand.][367034]} {[But sand dunes are actually dynamic natural structures.][367049]} {[They grow, shift and travel.][367058]} {[They crawl with living things.][367064]} {[Some sand dunes even sing.][367070]} {[A.][367076]} {[Although no more than a pile of wind-blown sand, dunes can roll over trees and buildings, march relentlessly across highways, devour vehicles on its path, and threaten crops and factories in Africa, the Middle East, and China.][367086]} {[In some places, killer dunes even roll in and swallow up towns.][367124]} {[Entire villages have disappeared under the sand.][367137]} {[In a few instances, the government built new villages for those displaced only to find that new villages themselves were buried several years later.][367145]} {[Preventing sand dunes from overwhelming cities and agricultural areas has become a priority for the United Nations Environment Program.][367169]} {[B.][367188]} {[Some of the most significant experimental measurements on sand movement were performed by Ralph Bagnold, a British engineer who worked in Egypt prior to World War II.][367208]} {[Bagnold investigated the physics of particles moving through the atmosphere and deposited by wind.][367235]} {[He recognised two basic dune types, the crescentic dune, which he called “barchan,” and the linear dune, which he called longitudinal or “sief ’ (Arabic for “sword”).][367250]} {[The crescentic barchan dune is the most common type of sand dune.][367261]} {[As its name suggests, this dune is shaped like a crescent moon with points at each end, and it is usually wider than it is long.][367274]} {[Some types of barchan dunes move faster over desert surfaces than any other type of dune.][367300]} {[The linear dune is straighter than the crescentic dune with ridges as its prominent feature.][367317]} {[Unlike crescentic dunes, linear dunes are longer than they are wide—in fact, some are more than 100 miles (about 160 kilometers) long.][367333]} {[Dunes can also be comprised of smaller dunes of different types, called complex dunes.][367354]} {[C. Despite the complicated dynamics of dune formation, Bagnold noted that a sand dune generally needs the following three things to form: a large amount of loose sand in an area with little vegetation—usually on the coast or in a dried-up river, lake or sea bed; a wind or breeze to move the grains of sand; and an obstacle, which could be as small as a rock or as big as a tree, that causes the sand to lose momentum and settle.][367369]} {[ Where these three variables merge, a sand dune forms.][367436]} {[D. As the wind picks up the sand, the sand travels, but generally only about an inch or two above the ground, until an obstacle causes it to stop.][367445]} {[The heaviest grains settle against the obstacle, and a small ridge or bump forms.][367471]} {[The lighter grains deposit themselves on the other side of the obstacle.][367484]} {[Wind continues to move sand up to the top of the pile until the pile is so steep that it collapses under its own weight.][367497]} {[The collapsing sand comes to rest when it reaches just the right steepness to keep the dune stable.][367523]} {[The repeating cycle of sand inching up the windward side to the dune crest, then slipping down the dune’s slip face allows the dune to inch forward, migrating in the direction the wind blows.][367542]} {[E. Depending on the speed and direction of the wind and the weight of the local sand, dunes will develop into different shapes and sizes.][367577]} {[Stronger winds tend to make taller dunes; gentler winds tend to spread them out.][367602]} {[If the direction of the wind generally is the same over the years, dunes gradually shift in that direction.][367617]} {[But a dune is “a curiously dynamic creature”, wrote Farouk El-Baz in National Geographic.][367637]} {[Once formed, a dune can grow, change shape, move with the wind and even breed new dunes.][367652]} {[Some of these offspring may be carried on the back of the mother dune.][367669]} {[Others are born and race downwind, outpacing their parents.][367680]} {[F. Sand dunes even can be heard ‘singing’ in more than 30 locations worldwide, and in each place the sounds have their own characteristic frequency, or note.][367690]} {[When the thirteenth century explorer Marco Polo encountered the weird and wonderful noises made by desert sand dunes, he attributed them to evil spirits.][367716]} {[The sound is unearthly.][367741]} {[The volume is also unnerving.][367747]} {[Adding to the tone’s otherworldliness is the inability of the human ear to localise the source of the noise.][367753]} {[Stéphane Douady of the French national research agency CNRS and his colleagues have been delving deeper into dunes in Morocco, Chile, China and Oman, and believe they can now explain the exact mechanism behind this acoustic phenomenon.][367773]}

{[G. The group hauled sand back to the laboratory and set it up in channels with automated pushing plates.][367815]} {[The sands still sang, proving that the dune itself was not needed to act as a resonating body for the sound, as some researchers had theorised.][367834]} {[To make the booming sound, the grains have to be of a small range of sizes, all alike in shape: well-rounded.][367860]} {[Douady’s key discovery was that this synchronised frequency — which determines the tone of sound — is the result of the grain size.][367881]} {[The larger the grain, the lower the key.][367906]} {[He has successfully predicted the notes emitted by dunes in Morocco, Chile and the US simply by measuring the size of the grains they contain.][367913]} {[Douady also discovered that the singing grains had some kind of varnish or a smooth coating of various minerals: silicon, iron and manganese, which probably formed on the sand when the dunes once lay beneath an ancient ocean.][367939]} {[But in the muted grains this coat had been worn away, which explains why only some dunes can sing.][367976]} {[He admits he is unsure exactly what role the coating plays in producing the noise.][367996]} {[The mysterious dunes, it seems, aren’t quite ready yet to give up all of their secrets.][368007]}

questionSets.instructionHtml:
Questions 1 - 7:

Reading passage 3 has seven paragraphs, A-G. Choose the correct heading for paragraphs A-G from the list of headings below.

Write the correct number, i-x, in boxes 1-7 on your answer sheet.

List of Headings

i      Shaping and reforming

ii     Causes of desertification

iii    Need combination of specific conditions

iv    Potential threat to industry and communication

v     An old superstition demystified

vi    Differences and similarities

vii   A continuous cycling process

viii  Habitat for rare species

ix    Replicating the process in laboratory

x     Commonest type of dune

questions.explanationHtml:
iv
 
Toàn bộ đoạn A nói về tác hại của "sand dune" - các đồi cát, có thể nuốt chửng cây cối, toà nhà, cao tốc và xe cộ, đe doạ đến mùa màng - "crops" và "factories" - nhà máy ở Châu Phi, Trung Đông và Trung Quốc.
--> Đồi cát là mối đe doạ tiềm tàng - "potential threat" cho sự giao tiếp và công nghiệp

x

 

Ralph Bagnold là kĩ sư người Anh làm việc ở Ai Cập vào thế chiến thứ 2. Ông ghi nhận có 2 loại đồi cát là

  1. Cresentic dune (hay còn gọi là barchan): đồi cát hình bán nguyệt

  2. Linear dune (hay còn gọi là "sief" - cây kiếm): đồi cát hình đường thẳng

Và cresentic dune là phổ biến nhất

iii

 

Đoạn này bàn về những "conditions" - điều kiện cần thiết để hình thành đồi cát. Cần 3 thứ

  1. Loose sand: cát bị lỏng, lún và rời rạc

  2. Wind: gió

Obstable: chướng ngại vật như là cây hoặc đá

vii

 

repeating = continuous: lặp đi lặp lại liên tục

Quá trình tạo ra các đồi cát là một chu trình lặp đi lặp lại, gió sẽ đẩy cát cao lên nhưng khi quá cao cát sẽ trồi sụt xuống và di chuyển về phía trước, sau đó gió lại đẩy cát cao lên và cứ thế.

i

 

reform (v) tái cấu trúc = grow, change shape

Dựa vào sức gió, hướng gió, và độ nặng của cát, đồi cát sẽ được tạo ra theo nhiều kích thước và hình dạng khác nhau. Đoạn này tập trung nói về hình dạng của đồi cát, cao hay thấp, và chúng di chuyển, thay đổi hình dáng như thế nào.

v

 

demystify (v) giải mã, làm sáng tỏ

Người ta đồn rằng các đồi cát có thể hát được. Đây chính là "old superstition" - điều mê tín dị đoan khi nhà thám hiểm Marco Polo nghe được những âm thanh này vào thế kỉ 13, ông cho rằng đây là âm thanh của "evil spirits" - linh hồn quỷ dữ. Ngày nay, Stephane đã có thể giải thích "mechanism" - cơ chế đằng sau việc này.

ix

 

replicate (v) mô phỏng, thực hiện lại

Để giải thích nguyên nhân vì sao các đồi cát có thể hát được, Stephane và các đồng nghiệp đã dựng lại đồi cát - "set it up" nhờ vào các đĩa đẩy - "pushing plates"

questionSets.contentHtml:
• 8 dune is said to have long ridges that can extend hundreds of miles.
  • According to Bagnold, an 9 is needed to stop the sand from moving before a dune can form.
  • Stéphane Douady believes the singing of dunes is not a spiritual phenomenon, but purely 10 

There are many different types of dunes, two of which are most commonly found in deserts throughout the world, the linear dune and the 11 dune, sometimes also known as the crescentic dune. It’s been long known that in some places dunes can even sing and the answer lies in the sand itself. To produce singing sand in lab, all the sands must have similar 12. And scientists have discovered that the size of the sand can affect the 13 of the sound. But the function of the varnish composed by a mixture of 14 still remains puzzling.
